There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one did not intend it, if one was unaware, if one was ill, if it was due to an emergency, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To sit scolded within a house constitutes a *duṣkṛta* (wrongdoing).
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one did not intend it, if one was unaware, if one was ill, if it was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To look around while entering a house is a *dukkaṭa* (offense of wrong-doing).
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To look around while sitting inside a house is a *duṣkṛta* (offense of wrong-doing).
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To enter a house making a loud noise is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one is insane, or if it was done previously.
To sit inside a house making a loud noise is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if there was no mindfulness, if there was ignorance, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To squat while entering a house is a *dukkaṭa* (offense of wrong-doing).
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
Entering a house with one's head covered is a duṣkṛta offense.

There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one was ill, if one was asleep, if there was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To sit inside a house with one's head covered is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense in cases of being asleep, insane, or having acted previously.
To enter a house exposing one's chest is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
Sitting with the chest exposed inside a house is a *duṣkṛta* (wrongdoing).

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one was ill, if one was asleep, if there was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To sit with one’s lower body hanging down inside a house is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one was ill, if one was asleep, if there was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously [before the rule was established].
To lift up one’s robe and enter a house, it is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one is insane, or if it was done previously.
To lift up one’s robe and sit inside a house, it is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one did not intend it, if one was unaware, if one was ill, if one was asleep, if there was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To swing one's arms while entering a house is a *dukkaṭa* (offense of wrong-doing).
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one is insane, or if it was done previously.
To sit shaking the body within a house is a *dukkaṭa* (offense of wrong-doing).

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one is ill, if one is asleep, if there is an urgent matter, if one is insane, or if it was done previously.
To shake one's head while entering a house is a *dukkaṭa*.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one was unaware, if one was insane, or if it was done previously [before the rule was established].
To sit inside a house shaking one's head is a *dukkaṭa*.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one was ill, if one was asleep, if there was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To poke or prod with hands or feet while entering a house is a *duṣkṛta* (offense of wrong-doing).
There is no offense if it was unintentional, done while insane, or previously committed.
To sit inside a house while playing with one's hands or feet is a *dukkaṭa*.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, done while insane, or previously committed.
To receive food with an unsteady hand is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one is insane, or if it was done previously.
To look left and right while receiving food is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
Taking too much soup is a *duṣkṛta* (offense of wrong-doing).

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one did not intend it, if one was unaware, if one was ill, if it was from various relatives, if one was invited, if it was for another or one’s own property, in an emergency, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To pile up rice into a mound is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously [before the rule was established].
To tear at the rice with the fingers while eating is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if there was no mindfulness, if there was ignorance, if one was ill, if the food was torn and left in one place, if it was an emergency, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To eat in a non-proper manner constitutes a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To gather food from various places and eat it constitutes a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one gathered while ill, if another gathered and brought it out for one, if it was an emergency, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To eat with excessive soup is a *duṣkṛta* (突吉羅).

There is no offense in the following cases: if it was not intentional; if one was not mindful; if one was unaware; if one was ill; if invited by various relatives; if it was one's own property; if it was for an urgent matter; if one was insane; or if it was done previously.
To knead a large mass [of dough] constitutes a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one was ill, if it concerned cakes or fruit, if it was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To repeatedly form a lump [of dough] constitutes a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one did not intend it, if one was unaware, if one was ill, if it was a cake or fruit, if there was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
If one clenches the mouth before it has reached [the food] and opens it, it is a *duṣkṛta* (offense of wrong-doing).
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one is insane, or if it was done previously.
If one speaks while holding rice in the mouth, it is a *duṣkṛta*.
There is no offense for one who is insane or for one who acted previously.
To put everything into the mouth is a *duṣkṛta*.
There is no offense for one who does not do so intentionally, or for one who is insane, or for one who acted previously; however, to make a smacking sound while eating is a *duṣkṛta*.
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To make a sucking sound while eating is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To lick the lips while eating is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one did not know, if one was ill, if it was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done previously [before the rule was established].
To eat with the tongue protruding is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one did not intend it, if one was unaware, if one was ill, if it was due to an emergency, if one was insane, or if it was done previously [when the rule was not yet established].
To eat with the nose wrinkled is a *duṣkṛta* offense.
There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one was insane, or if it was done previously.

To cause food to be spat out after having eaten it constitutes a *duṣkṛta* (offense of wrong-doing).

To seek out one's own soup and rice for oneself constitutes a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if there was no conscious thought [to do so], if one was unaware, if one was ill, if invited by a relative, if it was for another person, if it was one's own property, if it was due to an emergency, if one was insane, or if it was done previously [before the rule was established].
If the flavor of the soup covers the rice, it is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

There is no offense if it was unintentional, done while insane, or previously established.

There is no offense if it was unintentional, done while insane, or previously established.

There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one was unaware, if one was ill, if it was an urgent matter, if one was insane, or if it was done prior to the establishment of the rule.

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful [of the rule], if one did not know [the person’s state], if one’s hair was exposed due to illness, in cases of urgent business, if one was insane, or if it was done prior to the establishment of the rule.

There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one was insane, or if it was done previously [under different circumstances].

There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful [of the rule], if one was insane, or if it was done previously.
To preach the Dharma while wearing wooden clogs is a *duṣkṛta* (offense of wrong-doing).
There is no offense if it was not intentional, if one was not mindful [of the rule], if one was insane, or if it was done previously.

There is no offense if it was unintentional, if one was not mindful, if one was insane, or if it was done prior to the enactment of the rule.

To defecate, urinate, spit, or expectorate in water constitutes a *duṣkṛta* offense.
